title: Who creates it, who owns it
sub: Business architecture for data, the second series on enterprise architecture: who creates each of the business's concepts and who owns it, read from a matrix of what each capability creates, reads, updates and deletes; two capabilities that both create the account, and the business deciding which one does; owners who decide and stewards who look after each concept day to day; and an owner found by capability where nothing was written down.
howto: Glass in the layers' colours is the confirmed model: light gold is the strategy layer, where the capabilities sit, and salmon the information layer, where the business's concepts sit. In the matrix, C means a capability creates a concept, R that it reads it, U that it updates it and D that it deletes it. Gold marks an owner, who decides; sea-green a steward, who looks after a concept day to day; blue the data team. Rose is retail and blue the network. In the desert, blue is the water, and the people of the story are silhouettes.
